Ulupi.note: A Naga princess who wed Arjuna during his wanderings; mother of Iravan and, later, protector of the reborn Arjuna.

Iravan.note: Son of Arjuna and Ulupi; raised among the Nagas, he offered himself in sacrifice for the Pandava victory.

Kauravya.note: A king of the Nagas (serpent race); father of Ulupi.

Kadru.note: Daughter of Daksha, wife of Kashyap; mother of the nagas.

Vasuki.note: King of the nagas, son of Kashyap and Kadru; the serpent-rope of the ocean's churning.

Takshaka.note: A naga king, son of Kashyap and Kadru; his bite would one day slay Parikshit. Killed the king in fulfilment of a rishi's curse after Parikshit, hunting, had insulted a silent sage by hanging a dead snake round his neck; hid afterward from Parikshit's son Janamejaya's snake-sacrifice inside Indra's own court, and was saved along with Vasuki and the rest of his kind when Astika stopped the sacrifice at the last moment.

Shesha.note: Ananta, the endless serpent, son of Kashyap and Kadru, on whom Vishnu reclines.

Karkotaka.note: A great naga king, son of Kashyap and Kadru.

Airavata.note: A naga of Kadru's line (namesake of Indra's elephant).

Surasa.note: Daughter of Daksha, wife of Kashyap; a mother of serpents, and the sea-nagi who tested Hanuman's wit on the leap to Lanka.

Kaliya.note: The hundred-hooded serpent of the Yamuna, quelled when Krishna danced upon his hoods.

Aryaka.note: Naga elder; per the Mahabharata, kin who revived Bhima with nectar in the naga realm.

JaratkaruNagi.name: Jaratkaru
JaratkaruNagi.note: Sister of Vasuki, king of the nagas; given to the sage Jaratkaru, who shared her name, as the wife the prophecy demanded, to save both her own ancestors and the whole naga race from Janamejaya's sacrifice through their son Astika. MBh 1.13-16.

Astika.note: Son of the sage Jaratkaru and Vasuki's sister, also named Jaratkaru; interrupted Janamejaya's snake sacrifice with the nagas already falling into the fire, invoked as a boon before the king knew what he was granting, and stopped it with the serpents, Vasuki and Takshaka among them, saved mid-air. The frame the whole Mahabharata is recited inside. MBh 1.13-53.
